title: The Bag-and-Whisker Plot: A New Bagplot for Bivariate Data
summary: The paper addresses two limitations of the classical bagplot: a fixed inflation factor for outlier detection and an unstable convex-hull visualization of the fence. It recasts bivariate outlier detection as a multiple-testing problem using robust MCD-based Mahalanobis distances and χ²₂ p-values, then defines a data-adaptive fence via λ=max(λstat,λdata) with FWER/FDR/PFER control, and renders that fence directly with gradient whiskers. In the n=8 toy example all three error-control procedures flag only z8, and the final inflation factor is λ=8.

claims.statement: In the n=8 toy example, the final data-adaptive inflation factor is λ=8 under FWER and FDR control.
claims.config_for_value: Depth median z1=(7,5); MCD covariance diag(53/3,17); χ²₂ p-values; Holm-Bonferroni FWER q=0.1 and BH FDR q=0.1; λstat≈3.27, λdata=8.
claims.quote: For FWER and FDR, λ = max(3.27, 8) = 8.

claims.statement: In the same toy example, PFER control also yields final λ=8.
claims.config_for_value: Depth median z1=(7,5); MCD covariance diag(53/3,17); χ²₂ p-values; PFER q=0.5; λstat≈1.67, λdata=8.

claims.statement: In the toy example, the sole rejected observation across all three error-control procedures is z8.
claims.config_for_value: Holm-Bonferroni FWER q=0.1; BH FDR q=0.1; PFER q=0.5; χ²₂ p-values; MCD covariance; depth median z1.
claims.quote: In this example, the rejection set is identical across all three procedures, consisting solely of the extreme observation z8.

claims.statement: In the toy example, z8 has squared Mahalanobis distance d²=21.39.
claims.metric: squared Mahalanobis distance d² for z8
claims.config_for_value: Robust μ depth median z1=(7,5); MCD covariance diag(53/3,17); d²=(zi−μ)ᵀΣ⁻¹(zi−μ).

claims.statement: In the toy example, z8 has χ²₂ upper-tail p-value 2.27×10−5.
claims.config_for_value: χ²₂ reference distribution; d² for z8=21.39; p_i=P(χ²₂≥d²_i).

claims.statement: With the conventional fixed inflation factor 3, the original bagplot excludes four toy points (z5-z8) from its fence.
claims.metric: number of points excluded by fence
claims.config_for_value: Original Rousseeuw et al. bagplot; fixed inflation factor 3; n=8 toy data.
claims.quote: Applying the conventional fixed inflation factor of 3 to this dataset excludes four points (z5, z6, z7 and z8) from the fence.

claims.statement: Under bivariate normality the original bagplot's fixed factor 3 flags only 0.195% of observations.
claims.config_for_value: Original bagplot; fixed inflation factor 3; bivariate normal null distribution.
claims.quote: Under a bivariate normal distribution, however, the bagplot’s inflation factor of 3 results in only 0.195% of observations being outside of the fence.

match_target.why: The user hint specifically targets the toy example λ=8; C1 is the cheapest central target because it uses only n=8 data and exercises the full MCD→χ² p-value→multiple-testing→λ=max(λstat,λdata) pipeline, with C2/C3 confirming the same qualitative result under PFER and all three procedures.

tolerance.why: Rule 4: λ is an unbounded positive multiplier and the paper reports no standard deviation or CI for the toy example, so the prescribed 10% relative band applies.

requirements.stmt: Estimate the location parameter by the halfspace depth median.
requirements.quote: Specifically, we estimate the location vector μ with the depth median.

requirements.stmt: Estimate the covariance matrix with the Minimum Covariance Determinant (MCD) estimator.
requirements.quote: For the covariance matrix Σ, we employ the highly robust Minimum Covariance Determinant (MCD) estimator

requirements.stmt: Construct the bag as the central 50% deepest observations.
requirements.quote: we construct the central “bag” to contain about 50% of observations with the maximum halfspace depth.

requirements.stmt: Compute each point's squared Mahalanobis distance from the robust center using the robust covariance.
requirements.quote: we first measure its standardized distance from the robustly estimated center using the squared Mahalanobis distance

requirements.stmt: Convert each squared Mahalanobis distance to an upper-tail χ²₂ p-value.
requirements.quote: Under the null hypothesis H0i that an observation zi is not an outlier, its squared Mahalanobis distance can be compared to a χ2 2 distribution.

requirements.stmt: Apply a multiple-testing procedure at a specified error level q to obtain tadj.
requirements.quote: we apply a standard multiple testing procedure to control a desired error rate (e.g., FWER, FDR, PFER) at a specified level q.

requirements.stmt: Use Holm-Bonferroni for FWER at q=0.1, BH for FDR at q=0.1, and PFER at q=0.5.
requirements.quote: For FWER and FDR we set the nominal levels to 0.1. For PFER we set the nominal level to 0.5

requirements.stmt: Convert the adjusted significance threshold back to a squared Mahalanobis critical value d²adj.
requirements.quote: We then convert this threshold back to the critical value for the squared Mahalanobis distance

requirements.stmt: Define λstat using the median squared Mahalanobis distance as the scale for the bag boundary.
requirements.quote: Since the bag’s boundary represents the 50th percentile of data depth, it should correspond approximately to the median of the squared Mahalanobis distances.

requirements.stmt: Define λdata as the maximum magnification needed to enclose every non-rejected point.
Set the final inflation factor to λ=max(λstat,λdata).
requirements.quote: The final data-adaptive inflation factor λ is chosen to satisfy both the statistical criterion and the geometric constraint:

requirements.stmt: Draw the fence directly and flag exactly the points outside it.
requirements.quote: a point is flagged as an outlier if and only if it lies outside this line.

requirements.stmt: Draw individual whisker lines from the bag boundary to each outer point.
requirements.quote: Our approach draws individual lines from the bag’s boundary to each outer point

requirements.stmt: Use FAST-MCD with consistency scaling via the MASS cov.mcd implementation.
requirements.quote: we utilize this algorithm, including the necessary consistency scaling, via the cov.mcd function available in the MASS package in R.
Any hypothesis H0i with pi ≤tadj will be rejected.

data.name: Simulated normal-mixture datasets (Examples 1-2)
data.how_to_get: Generate from the Section 5 equations: n=5000, Bernoulli(0.05) mixture with μ0=(100,300), μ1=(103,298), I2 or correlation 0.3; set a seed because none is given.

data.name: Simulated log-normal dataset (Example 3)
data.how_to_get: Generate n=500 independent log-normal(0,0.5) coordinates as in Section 5; set a seed because none is given.
